lead.tldr: US seizure of nearly $1bn crypto from Iran heightens enforcement risk for sanctioned jurisdictions • OKX Ventures and Korea Investment each invest $53m for 19.6% stake in Coinone, pending approval • CFTC greenlights regulated Bitcoin perpetual futures, opening institutional margin collateral and clearing pathways • Hyperliquid’s volume surpasses Nasdaq, but offshore status may trigger regulatory scrutiny across jurisdictions • Spot Bitcoin ETFs face $2.8bn nine‑day outflows, signaling short‑term investor fatigue amid price decline

intro: Dear Founders, Investors, and Friends, U.S. authorities have seized nearly $1 billion linked to Iran, underscoring heightened regulatory scrutiny. Meanwhile, OKX Ventures' $53 million stake in Korea’s Coinone and the CFTC’s approval of regulated Bitcoin perpetual futures highlight fresh capital inflows and market maturation.

top_signals.title: US has seized nearly $1 billion in crypto from Iran, Bessent says
top_signals.summary: U.S. authorities have seized almost $1 billion worth of cryptocurrency that was linked to Iran, according to a statement from Bessent. The assets were taken as part of the United States’ ongoing enforcement of sanctions targeting Iran’s illicit crypto operations. The action underscores the heightened regulatory scrutiny of cross‑border digital‑asset transactions and signals that institutional investors must maintain robust compliance frameworks when dealing with counterparties in sanctioned jurisdictions.

top_signals.title: OKX Ventures buys $53 million stake in Korea's Coinone exchange
top_signals.summary: OKX Ventures and Korea Investment & Securities each invested 80 billion won, roughly $53 million, for a combined 19.6 % stake in the South Korean cryptocurrency exchange Coinone. The $106 million transaction is pending regulatory approval. With the investment, OKX Ventures and Korea Investment & Securities become joint third‑largest shareholders of Coinone. CEO Cha Myunghun remains the largest shareholder and retains management control, which may influence the exchange’s strategic direction and governance.

top_signals.title: Hyperliquid ETF negotiates new investment, How Asia's crypto future may look, Myriad launches World Cup competition
top_signals.summary: Grayscale is negotiating to sell shares of its Hyperliquid Staking ETF for roughly 2 million HYPE tokens, valued at about $115 million. This transaction could provide liquidity and exposure to a staking‑focused product for institutional portfolios. The report also highlights TRON’s position as the largest holder of USDT, underscoring the network’s role in stablecoin circulation. Additionally, Myriad has launched a $100 k World Cup prediction‑market competition, reflecting growing interest in crypto‑driven sports betting and broader Asian market dynamics.

top_signals.title: The CFTC Greenlights Crypto Perps in America on Bankless
top_signals.summary: The Commodity Futures Trading Commission has approved KalshiEX’s BTCPERP, establishing the first regulated Bitcoin perpetual futures contract in the United States. In a complementary action the CFTC issued a no‑action letter that permits Coinbase to direct U.S. customers to Deribit for access to global crypto derivatives markets. The approvals allow Bitcoin, Ethereum and stablecoins to be used as margin collateral on regulated platforms. Institutional investors view the development as a historic step toward broader adoption of crypto derivatives within the mainstream financial system.

top_signals.title: The fastest growing legaltech startup teams in Europe
top_signals.summary: Sifted reports rapid expansion across European legal‑tech startups, with 36 firms hiring aggressively and several achieving over 200% staff growth, notably unicorn Legora. The sector’s momentum is highlighted by Lexroom’s $50 million Series B round led by Left Lane Capital, which signals strong investor confidence. This hiring surge and capital inflow suggest that legal‑tech teams are scaling quickly, making the space attractive for institutional capital seeking growth opportunities.

top_signals.title: Bitcoin ETFs suffer record 9-day outflow streak as $2.8 billion exits funds
top_signals.summary: U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs have recorded a nine‑day streak of net outflows, with about $2.8 billion withdrawn. The withdrawals align with a recent decline in Bitcoin’s price and heightened institutional selling pressure. The trend was highlighted by BlackRock’s iShares Bitcoin Trust registering its largest single‑day redemption, underscoring the sensitivity of ETF inflows to market sentiment.

top_signals.title: ICE CEO calls Hyperliquid bigger than NASDAQ, says he's met its founders
top_signals.summary: ICE chief executive Jeffrey Sprecher said Hyperliquid’s decentralized perpetual futures platform now trades more volume than the Nasdaq exchange. He noted that the platform commands over 70 percent of the perpetual‑DEX market. Sprecher also pointed to Hyperliquid’s 24/7 oil derivatives offering as a differentiator. He warned that the platform’s offshore, unregulated status creates a regulatory gap that policymakers will need to address.

top_signals.title: Paxos wins SEC approval to clear U.S. stocks on blockchain
top_signals.summary: Paxos Securities Settlement Company has received full registration from the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission, making it the first blockchain‑based central securities depository authorized to clear U.S. equities. The approval places Paxos on equal regulatory footing with established post‑trade infrastructure providers such as the Depository Trust & Clearing Corporation. Institutional investors can now access near‑instant settlement of stock trades on a blockchain platform, potentially reducing settlement risk and operational costs.

linkedin_post: Dear Founders, Investors, and Friends, The past week has reminded us why vigilance, partnership and innovation remain at the heart of the crypto ecosystem. In the United States, authorities seized almost $1 billion of digital assets linked to Iran. The move highlights the growing regulatory focus on cross‑border transactions and reinforces the need for robust compliance frameworks when dealing with sanctioned parties. For European investors this is a clear signal to embed thorough due‑diligence processes in every deal. Across the Pacific, OKX Ventures and Korea Investment & Securities each placed roughly $53 million into Coinone, together acquiring a 19.6 percent stake. The investment makes them joint third‑largest shareholders while the founding CEO retains control. This partnership illustrates how strategic capital can unlock growth in mature Asian exchanges without disrupting existing leadership. Meanwhile, Grayscale is negotiating the sale of shares in its Hyperliquid Staking ETF for about 2 million HYPE tokens, a transaction that could bring $115 million of liquidity to institutional portfolios. The same report notes that TRON now holds the largest share of USDT, underscoring its role in stablecoin circulation. In a lighter vein, Myriad has launched a $100 k World Cup prediction market competition, showing the rising appetite for crypto‑driven sports betting in Asia. At Blockwall we see these developments as proof that the market is maturing, that capital is flowing strategically, and that compliance, governance and creative use‑cases will shape the next wave.
